DERECHO DILG-CARAGA Administrative Region Matimco Bldg., Km. 4, Libertad Butuan City Dear Director Derecho: This refers to your request for legal opin•o relative to the commencement of the corporate existence of the Province of D nagat Islands, a newly created province by virtue of RA 9355 (An Act Creating h Province of Dinagat Islands). Sections 49, 50 and 51 of RA 9355 provi e hat: "SEC. 49. Commencement of o orate Existence.- The Province of Dinagat Islands shall c mmence its corporate existence upon the election and qualific on of the governor, vice governor and majority of the mem e s of the sangguniang panlalawigan. " "SEC. 50. Officials of the Provin e f Dinagat Islands.- (A) The first set of elective officials of the P o ince of Dinagat Islands shall be elected in the next local electio s ollowing the effectivity of this Act. The President of the Philippines s all appoint an interim governor, vice governor and memb r of the sangguniang panlalawigan, who shall serve only un 'l a new set of provincial officials have been elected and qualified. ' "SEC. 51. Organization of the Pr v •ncial Government.- All provincial appointive positions in the o ince of Dinagat Islands

-2 as enumerated in Section 8 hereof shall b filled within sixty (60) days after the commencement of co rate existence of the province, as provided for in Section 49 of. This shall be done without prejudice to the officials and ployees of the present Province of Surigao del Norte, who a wish to serve in the Province of Dinagat Islands." With the abovequoted provisions of A 9355, you now wish to be enlightened on whether or not the corporat xistence of the province will commence: (a) upon the appointment by the P e ident of the Philippines of the interim governor, vice governor and members f he sangguniang panlalawigan; or (b) upon the election and qualification of t e governor and majority of the members of the sangguniang panlalawigan. Before replying to your query, mayw uote Section 14 of the Local Government, which is the general law with resp t to local governments, to wit: "SEC. 14. Beginning of Corporat istence.- When a new local government unit is created, its o orate existence shall commence upon the election and qualific on of its chief executive and a majority of the members of its san nian, unless some other time is fixed therefor by the law or ordin n creating it." It, therefore, becomes imperative for us t discuss the rules of statutory construction as applied to statutes in relation to t er statutes. One of these rules is the in pari materia rule. Statutes or laws in p materia refer to "those which are related to the same person or thing, or to th s me class of persons or things, or which have a common purpose or object" (2 S therland, Stat. Const., 3rd, ed., p. 535). "All laws are presumed to have been en c ed by the legislature with full knowledge of the existing condition of the law a with reference to it. They are, therefore, to be construed in connection with a d in harmony with the existing law and as a part ofa general and uniform ju s rudence" (Storis vs. Heck, 190 So. 86). "The in pari materia rule of co ruction decrees that in the construction ofa particular statute, or in thein e retation of its provisions, all statutes relating to the same general purpose s o ld be read in connection with it. Statutes in pari materia should be construct d s if they constituted one law, or one system enacted in the sante spirit infu h ance of the same policy" (82 C.J.S., pp. 803-806). "Hence, the legislative int is not to be derived from the literal meaning of the words of a statute but fr a view of the whole system of which it is a part" (Smith vs. Higginbottom, 48 A Yd., p. 754). "Therefore, the purpose of the in pari materia rule of cons tion is to carry out the full legislative intent by giving effect to all laws an rovisions bearing on the same

-3 subject" (Texas, et al. vs. Kelso, etc., 250 S.W., p. 425). Along this line, it is relevant to not hat Section 14 of the Local Government Code provides for the general rule t at the corporate existence of a local government unit shall commence upon th lection and qualification of its chief executive and a majority of the members f its sanggunian. Said provision, however, is immediately followed by an except o , i.e., "unless some other time is fixed therefor by the law or ordinance creatin i To harmonize this with RA 9355, as clea y he laws are in pari materia, it is noted that Section 49 of RA 9355 provides fo e general rule with respect to the commencement of corporate existence of t Province of Dinagat Islands which was also the general rule found in Sect•0 14 of the Local Government Code. Section 50 of RA 9355, however, pro id d for the transitory provision where the President was empowered by the I itself to appoint the interim governor, vice governor and members of the sa g uniang panlalawigan who shall serve only until a new set of provincial officials h ve been elected and qualified. This is understandable because under the first p ragraph of Section 50 of RA 9355, it is mandated that the first set of electiv o ficials of the province shall be elected in the next local elections following the ff ctivity of the Act. Corollarily, since the Act was approve n 02 October 2006 and the subsequent plebiscite was conducted which res It d to its ratification, the logical conclusion would be that the first set of electi e local officials shall be elected come 14 May 2007 elections. At this point i bears to state the doctrinal pronouncement of the Supreme Court in the casF f "Mejia yy. Balolong" (81 Phil. 486), where the court ruled that the City of Dåg pan came into existence as a legal entity or public corporation upon approva o said Act creating it. But as a city is a public corporation or a juridical entit nd as such cannot operate or transact business by itself but through its agents o officers, it was necessary that the officials thereof be appointed or elected in or er that it may act or transact business as such public corporation or city. The S preme Court saw the necessity that the city government be organized since atc rding to the highest court, to create a public corporation is one thing and to o g nize the government thereof is another. With the Supreme Court pronounceme t in the aforecited case, taken along with the exception provided under Secti 14 of the Local Government Code, it does becomes obvious that the intentio f Congress in empowering the President to appoint the set of interim elective Io al officials of Dinagat Islands pending the election of the first set of its local I ctive officials in the next local elections following the effectivity of the law cr ating the province is to confer

-4- upon the province its immediate corporate ex st nce so that the province can already normally operate as a political subdivtsi n of the State bestowed with corporate and governmental powers for the ben fi of its constituents. This is the common purpose that could be seen in har izing Section 14 of the Local Government Code and Sections 49 and 50 of R 355. The conferment unto the President of the power to appoint the interim t f local elective officials should be taken as an exception to the general rule o nd in Section 14 of the Local Government Code. Taking, therefore, the legislative intent o t e law, we are of the view that the corporate existence of the Province of Di a at Islands should be reckoned from the appointment by the President of the in e im set of local elective officials thereat. With respect to Section 51 of RA 9355, believe that in line with our disquisition above, and to further give signi ic nce to the reason why the legislature gave the President the power to appo nt the interim set of local elective officials, we believe that the interim set of loc I elective officials of Dinagat Islands can already exercise those powers as ar c nferred by RA 9355, the Local Government Code and other existing laws and h se that are implied therefrom, including the power to appoint, by organizing th rovincial government pursuant to Section 51 of RA 9355 within 60 days after th ommencement of its corporate existence which, to our mind, has to be r c oned from the time of the appointment of the interim set of local officials. We hope to have enlightened you on the a ter. Very truly yours, ASEC AUSTERE RO OIC-OUSLCY d/ Legal:43/La
